subject: Approval: Marketplace SKU pricing + discount guidance (AWS/GCP)
body:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 28, 2025 at 8:42 AM
Subject: Approval: Marketplace SKU pricing + discount guidance (AWS/GCP)

Jordan — we need GTM leadership approval on the marketplace pricing/discount policy before we finalize the AWS/GCP submissions.

Key decisions to approve (proposed):
1) Floor pricing guardrails on marketplace SKUs (Hosted API / Dedicated / Private) to offset marketplace fees + revrec constraints.
2) Discounting policy: what can be offered via private offers, who approves what, and when we route to direct contracts.
3) Field guidance: a simple “use marketplace vs direct” decision tree for AEs/SEs.

Attachments:
- Marketplace_Discounting_and_Channel_Guidance_v0.9.pdf
- Marketplace_SKU_Pricing_Guardrails_v2.xlsx

If you approve, Soojin will incorporate into sales enablement + listing FAQ language, and Finance/Legal will align internal quoting guidance.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Finance Sponsor, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 28, 2025 at 9:11 AM
Subject: Re: Approval: Marketplace SKU pricing + discount guidance (AWS/GCP)

Thanks. I’m aligned in principle but want to make sure this doesn’t tie the field’s hands.

Two questions before I sign:
- Are we explicitly allowing Private Offers (AWS) / Private Offers (GCP) for enterprise procurement (so AEs can match a direct quote structure)?
- Where are we drawing the line on “marketplace vs direct” for Private (VPC/on-prem) and premium SLA add-on?

If you can answer those cleanly, I’ll approve today.

Jordan

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 28, 2025 at 9:46 AM
Subject: Re: Approval: Marketplace SKU pricing + discount guidance (AWS/GCP)

Answering w/ Finance lens:

1) Private offers: Yes. The policy assumes enterprise deals go through Private Offers when they need PO/invoice + committed spend on AWS/GCP. We’re not forcing “public list price only.”

2) Marketplace vs direct (proposed decision line):
- Marketplace is preferred when the buyer’s primary requirement is cloud commit drawdown / procurement convenience and they can accept standard marketplace terms.
- Direct is preferred when we need: (a) non-standard legal terms beyond what marketplace supports, (b) deep discount beyond guardrails, (c) complex multi-year with custom ramp + services, or (d) any on-prem / air-gapped Private package that is not delivered as a marketplace-integrated deployment.

Why the guardrails:
- Marketplace fees effectively reduce our net; the floors in the spreadsheet keep us from accidentally going negative margin on high-throughput Hosted and Dedicated workloads.

If it’s helpful, we can add a one-liner for the field: “If Legal redlines are required, default to direct.”

Rishi

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 28, 2025 at 10:18 AM
Subject: Re: Approval: Marketplace SKU pricing + discount guidance (AWS/GCP)

From Legal:

- Marketplace path is fine for standard enterprise procurement, but we should be explicit: we can’t negotiate core marketplace terms the way we can a direct MSA + DPA. Some customers will ask for custom liability, SCCs addenda, bespoke audit rights, or “no unilateral changes” clauses. Those should go direct.

- For Private (VPC): acceptable via marketplace if it’s our standard VPC deployment and the customer can sign the marketplace EULA and our addenda as published (no redlines). For on-prem/air-gapped: direct.

- Premium SLA: can be sold as a marketplace add-on SKU if it’s the standard SLA language. Any bespoke SLA (penalties beyond our standard, custom SLOs, unique remedies) should be direct.

If you approve, I’d like Soojin to include “Standard terms only via marketplace” in the internal talk track so AEs don’t overpromise.

Michael Grant
Legal Sponsor

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 28, 2025 at 11:02 AM
Subject: Re: Approval: Marketplace SKU pricing + discount guidance (AWS/GCP)

Jordan — we’ll translate this into a simple field-ready decision tree + one slide.

Proposed wording for Sales/SE:

Use marketplace when:
- Buyer needs AWS/GCP commit drawdown / prefers marketplace invoicing
- They can accept standard terms (no redlines)
- They want fast procurement + immediate activation

Push direct contract when:
- Custom legal terms / redlines are required
- Discount request exceeds marketplace guardrails
- Complex multi-year ramps / services-heavy package
- On-prem or air-gapped Private
- Bespoke SLA requirements

Discounting (internal):
- Marketplace: standard list price OR private offer within approved bands
- Approvals: AE manager for small adjustments; Finance + Jordan for anything material; Legal only when moving to direct

If approved, I’ll update the enablement deck + FAQ and align with the listing FAQ so we don’t say anything that conflicts.

Soojin

Subject: Re: Approval: Marketplace SKU pricing + discount guidance (AWS/GCP)

+1. From a marketing perspective, the “standard terms only” point is important for expectation setting.

Jordan — the only thing I’d add is a clear sentence for AEs: marketplace is not “second class.” It’s our preferred procurement path when the buyer wants cloud commit alignment.

Camila

Date: Tue, Jan 28, 2025 at 12:09 PM
Subject: Re: Approval: Marketplace SKU pricing + discount guidance (AWS/GCP)

Approved with two tweaks:

1) Make the escalation threshold unambiguous for the field.
- Any request beyond approved discount band OR any “custom terms” request = route to direct evaluation and loop Finance + Legal.

2) Add one more “push direct” bullet:
- If the customer needs consolidated pricing across multiple cloud providers/regions with a single commercial schedule (we’ve seen this a few times). Marketplace can get messy.

Otherwise: yes, we should actively recommend marketplace when the customer’s procurement is cloud-commit driven.

Laura/Rishi — please finalize the policy doc and circulate for enablement.

Jordan Blake
GTM Executive Sponsor
